challenges.name: The Solar System Signal
challenges.tip: Explain a science idea in your own words. If you can teach it, you probably understand it.

questions.q: Which planet has the largest number of confirmed moons?
questions.why: Saturn currently has the most confirmed moons.

questions.q: What force keeps planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.why: The Sun's gravity keeps planets moving in their orbits.

questions.q: Which layer of Earth is liquid and helps create its magnetic field?
questions.why: Movement in the liquid outer core helps generate Earth's magnetic field.

challenges.name: The Fraction Vault
challenges.tip: For fractions, make denominators the same before adding or subtracting.

questions.q: What is 3/4 of 20?
Which fraction is equal to 0.5?
questions.why: One half is the same as 0.5 or 50%.

questions.q: What is 2/3 + 1/3?
questions.why: The denominators match, so add the numerators: 3/3 = 1.

challenges.name: The Geography Compass
challenges.tip: Use a compass rose to check directions before describing a route.

questions.q: Which line divides Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
questions.why: The Equator is at 0° latitude and divides the two hemispheres.

questions.q: What does a map scale help you calculate?
questions.why: A scale compares map distance with actual distance.

questions.q: Which direction is opposite to south-east?
questions.why: The opposite direction across the compass is north-west.

challenges.name: The Biology Lab Mystery
challenges.tip: Remember: producers make their own food, while consumers obtain energy by eating.

questions.q: Which part of a plant mainly absorbs water from the soil?
questions.why: Root hairs absorb water and mineral ions from the soil.

questions.q: What is the main function of red blood cells?
questions.why: Haemoglobin in red blood cells carries oxygen around the body.

questions.q: Which organisms break down dead material?
questions.why: Fungi and bacteria are important decomposers in ecosystems.

challenges.name: The Algebra Lock
challenges.tip: Collect like terms only when their variable parts match exactly.

questions.q: Simplify: 4x + 3x
questions.why: Add the coefficients: 4x + 3x = 7x.

questions.q: Solve: x + 6 = 14
questions.why: Subtract 6 from both sides to get x = 8.

questions.q: Expand: 3(y + 2)
questions.why: Multiply both terms by 3: 3y + 6.

challenges.name: The Energy Investigation
challenges.tip: Energy is transferred between stores; it is not created or destroyed.

questions.q: What type of energy is stored in a stretched spring?
questions.why: A stretched or compressed spring stores elastic potential energy.

questions.q: Which material is usually a good electrical conductor?
questions.why: Copper is a metal and allows electric charge to flow easily.

questions.q: What happens to a light ray when it reflects?
questions.why: Reflection is when light bounces off a surface.

challenges.name: The Logic Detective
challenges.tip: A good conclusion must be supported by the clues, not just by a guess.

questions.q: All squares are rectangles. A shape is a square. What must be true?
questions.why: If every square is a rectangle, every square has the properties of a rectangle.

questions.q: A bus leaves at 09:20 and arrives at 10:05. How long is the journey?
questions.why: From 09:20 to 10:00 is 40 minutes, then 5 more minutes.

questions.q: Which number completes the pattern: 3, 6, 12, 24, __?
questions.why: Each number is doubled, so 24 × 2 = 48.
